doc.summary: Keyless CVE intelligence feeds and version-aware service correlation.
doc.description:
Correlates discovered services against public exploit intelligence with
no account and no API key, then grades every candidate with a
deterministic heat tier (see :mod:`modules.lazy_heat`):

  cisa_kev    CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (JSON)
  epss        FIRST EPSS probability scores (daily CSV, gzipped)
  exploit_db  Exploit-DB public exploit index (CSV)
  metasploit  Metasploit module metadata (JSON)
  osv         OSV.dev advisories for version ranges (per-product, cached)

A source only ever adds evidence: being absent from one source never
clears what another reported. Every download is bounded, cached on disk
under ``sessions/cve_feed/`` with its own TTL, and every entry point
degrades to empty results when the network or the feed is unavailable,
so the autonomous loop never stalls on intelligence.

Stdlib only.

signature: def load_kev(force: bool = False) -> dict[str, dict]

doc.summary: Return ``{cve_id: {product, vendor}}`` from the CISA KEV catalog.

params.name: force
params.description: Re-download even when the cache is fresh.

returns.description: Mapping keyed by upper CVE id; empty when offline.

params.description: Re-download even when the cache is fresh.

returns.description: Mapping keyed by upper CVE id; empty when offline.

name: fetch_product_advisories
signature: def fetch_product_advisories(product: str, force: bool = False) -> list[dict]

doc.summary: Fetch OSV advisories naming one product.
doc.description:
The query endpoint requires an ecosystem, so candidate package
names (each banner word plus the joined token) are tried against
each candidate distro ecosystem and the answers merged; the merged
set is cached per product with the OSV TTL.

params.name: product
params.description: Product text as found on a banner (``Samba smbd 3.0.20``).

params.name: force
params.description: Re-query even when the cache is fresh.

returns.description: List of advisory dicts with ``affected`` ranges; [] offline.

name: cve_intel
signature: def cve_intel(cve_id: str, feeds: dict | None = None, allow_network: bool = True) -> dict

doc.summary: Assemble exploitation signals and the heat tier for one CVE.

params.name: feeds
params.description: Preloaded feeds (``kev``/``epss``/``exploit``/``msf``); loaded lazily when None.

params.name: allow_network
params.description: Allow feed downloads on a cold cache.

name: correlate
signature: def correlate(product: str, version: str = '', allow_network: bool = True) -> list[dict]

doc.summary: Version-aware CVE candidates for one service product.
doc.description:
Candidates come from OSV advisories (which carry affected version
ranges) filtered by :func:`version_in_range`, plus KEV product
matches KEV lists under the same vendor product. Every candidate is
heat-graded; a match inside the affected range reads as affected.

params.name: allow_network
params.description: Allow OSV queries on a cold cache.

returns.description:
List of ``{"cve", "heat", "cvss", "kev", "epss", "exploit",
"in_range", "confidence", "severity"}`` sorted hottest first,
capped at :data:`CORRELATE_CAP`.

name: load_kev_matches
signature: def load_kev_matches(product: str, feeds: dict | None = None) -> list[tuple[str, dict]]

doc.summary: KEV entries whose vendor/product names match one service product.
doc.description:
Matching is word-level: a banner like ``Samba smbd 3.0.20`` matches
the KEV product ``Samba`` without demanding the whole banner token.

params.name: product
params.description: Banner product/version text (not a normalised token).

params.name: feeds
params.description: Preloaded KEV mapping; loaded when None.

returns.description: List of ``(cve, intel)`` pairs, hottest first.

name: hot_matches
signature: def hot_matches(services: list[dict], allow_network: bool = False) -> list[dict]

doc.summary: Hot/warm CVE candidates matching discovered services.
doc.description:
Built for the loop's ``cve_hot`` trigger: each service row carries
``name``/``product``/``version`` and every returned row carries the
service context so the planner can target verification intents.

params.name: allow_network
params.description: Allow OSV queries on a cold cache.

name: refresh_feeds_async
signature: def refresh_feeds_async(products: list[str] | None = None) -> None

doc.summary: Refresh bulk feeds in one background daemon thread.
doc.description:
Call once per process (idempotent): KEV, EPSS, Exploit-DB and
Metasploit re-download only when their TTL expired, and each
product gets one OSV prefetch so later cache-only correlations
find candidates without blocking the pipeline on network.

params.name: products
params.description: Banner strings to prefetch OSV advisories for.
